items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: I didn’t realize until then this was down by Inische [sic], and we had a separate community.

ctx.x: Well China and Japan — my history is not great — but they’ve had a checkered history over the years. Was it difficult to go from one to the other?

No. Because we all did it — what they call they have a Japanese school. The Japanese community is quite different from the Chinese community. We were in a Japanese community. You know a funny thing about it — 30 years ago I was back in China, now they call it the Yunnan Province old Manchuria, and I visited my own, where I was born, where I went to school, and I didn’t realize until then this was down by Inische [sic], and we had a separate community. You know I was too little to realize that. My father’s right…
I’ve been told that. It’s one of the hardest. What was your exposure to music before you moved to Japan?
